blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing supply chain risk at the intermediate level means moving from a vague list of things that could go wrong to a specific, scored, live risk register that changes as the world changes. Each risk is rated for likelihood and impact. Each one has an owner. Each one has a planned response, rehearsed at least in conversation, so that nobody is inventing a solution at 2 a.m.

The register is not a document to admire. It is a working tool. Risks are added, closed, re-scored and escalated. When something goes wrong, the response is not improvised — it is already written, just pulled off the shelf and adapted to the situation in front of you.

A good risk register does not prevent crises. It prevents panic. That is often worth far more than the register itself.

items.q: According to the text, what should a live risk register do?
options: Stay unchanged once it is signed off
items.why: "a live risk register that changes as the world changes."

items.q: What does the text say each risk must have?
options: A budget line and a deadline
A likelihood score, an owner and a planned response
items.why: "rated for likelihood and impact… has an owner… has a planned response."

items.q: What does "pulled off the shelf and adapted" suggest about the response to a crisis?
options: It is invented on the spot
It is prepared in advance and then adjusted
It is bought from an outside supplier
items.why: Inferência: 'off the shelf' significa que já estava pronta — só é adaptada, não improvisada.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A risk register is only useful if people keep updating it
Rehearsing a response makes a real crisis easier to handle
A well-written register on the shelf is enough on its own
Preventing panic can matter more than the document itself
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que o registro é 'a working tool', não 'a document to admire'.

items.q: The text says the register "prevents panic" rather than crises. This suggests that…
options: the value lies in a calm, ready response, not in stopping bad events
crises can be avoided entirely with good planning
the register is mainly a legal requirement
panic and crises are the same thing
items.why: Inferência: não dá para evitar toda crise; o ganho é reagir com calma em vez de entrar em pânico.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte falando com a equipe enquanto reconstrói o registro de riscos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, thanks for making the time. I want to be honest about why we are back here. When the supplier went bankrupt last month, we had a risk register that mentioned exactly this scenario. It was documented. And yet, on the day, half the team had never read it, and the rest of us were improvising responses at midnight.

So the register was technically fine and completely useless at the same time. That gap is what we are fixing today, not the wording.

From now on, every risk should be scored for likelihood and impact, and every risk must have a named owner. Not a department — a person. That owner should rehearse the response with me at least once a quarter, even if it is only a ten-minute conversation.

And the register will be reviewed every month, and updated immediately after any real event. If a supplier wobbles, we re-score that risk the same week. A response that can be pulled off the shelf and adapted is always calmer than one invented under pressure. That is the whole point.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why are the team back to rebuild the risk register?
options: A new regulation requires a different format
The scenario was documented, but the team still improvised on the day
The register never mentioned the bankruptcy scenario
items.why: "a risk register that mentioned exactly this scenario… and yet… we were improvising responses at midnight."

items.q: According to Charlotte, who must own each risk?
options: A named person, not a department
items.why: "every risk must have a named owner. Not a department — a person."

items.q: How often should the owner rehearse the response with Charlotte?
items.why: "rehearse the response with me at least once a quarter."

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "technically fine and completely useless at the same time"?
options: The document existed but did not change what people did
The software crashed on the day
The register was too short to be useful
items.why: Inferência: existir no papel não adianta se ninguém leu nem agiu com base nele.

items.q: What is Charlotte's main priority in this meeting?
options: Finding a new supplier as fast as possible
Reducing the number of risks on the list
Closing the gap between the document and what the team actually does
Improving the wording of the register
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que o problema é o 'gap', 'not the wording' — o foco é a prática, não o texto.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We need to score each risk before the review." To score a risk means to…
options: rate it, usually for likelihood and impact
items.why: To score = pontuar, atribuir uma nota (aqui, por probabilidade e impacto).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A port strike has low ___ this month, but the impact would be severe."
items.why: Likelihood = probabilidade — o quanto é provável que algo aconteça.

items.q: "Every risk needs an owner." In this context, an owner is…
options: the person responsible for that risk and its response
the supplier who caused the risk
the author of the original report
items.why: Owner = responsável designado por aquele risco (não é o dono da empresa).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Because the plan was ___, the team stayed calm when the supplier failed."
items.why: Rehearsed = ensaiado; uma resposta ensaiada mantém a equipe calma.

items.q: "They had to improvise a response at midnight." To improvise means to…
options: create a solution on the spot, without preparation
follow a written plan step by step
items.why: To improvise = improvisar, criar na hora sem preparo prévio.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de gestão de risco. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The response can be pulled off the shelf and adapted." Something off the shelf is…
options: already prepared and ready to use
items.why: Off the shelf = pronto, já disponível para usar (só adaptar).

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the new register." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new process to every site." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar, colocar em prática (muitas vezes por etapas).

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on the monthly reviews." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to rehearse the plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to completion
carried it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não levaram.
